Thank you Edward, it worked in R studio...
But I am still stuck with this one (attempt to run a multilevel sem with mediation analysis)

modelsem <- '
        level: 1
            evs=~ KH1 + KH2 + KH3 + KH4
    dub=~ KH5 + KH6 + KH7 + KH8
    rat=~ KH9 + KH10 + KH11 + KH12
            wel=~ PW1 + PW2 + PW3 + PW4 + PW5 + PW6 + PW7
          wel~ a1*evs + a2*dub + a3*rat
        level: 2
            rjp=~ IRP1 + IRP2 + IRP3 + IRP4 + IRP5
    rjp~ c11*rat + c21*evs + c31*dub + b1*wel
            inp=~ INN1 + INN2 + INN3 + INN4 + INN5 + INN6 + INN7
    inp~ c12*rat + c22*evs + c32*dub + b2*wel

        indirect := a1*b1
        direct := c1
        total := c1 + (a1*b1)

        evs~~dub
        evs~~rat
        dub~~rat
    '
fitsem <- sem(model = modelsem, data = know2, cluster = "supnumb")
summary(fitsem)

The CFA works well but here, while introducing regression, latent variables are not recognized.

Error in lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: missing observed variables in dataset: rat eva dum wel

Help please.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: ERROR: model is NULL!
parts: In addition, you have these lines in the level 2 block:
rjp~ c11*rat + c21*evs + c31*dub + b1*wel
inp~ c12*rat + c22*evs + c32*dub + b2*wel

but the (level-1 latent variables) rat/evs/du/wel do not exist at the
second level.

If you need a level-2 version of these latent variables, you need to
define them at the level-2 first, before you use them in a regression
(at level 2).

Yves.
